profile.mgmt: Binod Kumar (MD & CEO — left at 6:30pm) · Ashutosh Choudhury, Shiv Bajrang Singh, Mini T M (Executive Directors) · Sunil Jain (CFO) · hosted by Nuvama Wealth (Anand Dama)

deepdive.sec: Banking / Public Sector Bank (large-cap PSU bank)

bull_bear.body:
- CAR 17.58% / CET1 16.51% (IFR Rs.2,000 cr Tier2→Tier1 = +44 bps) — comfortably capitalised, no raise flagged.
- Building buffers: **Rs.1,000 cr floating ECL provision** + **Rs.310 cr West Asia** provision carried (Rs.13 cr top-up); PCR held at 98.22% (could have been higher but chose to let NNPA sit at 0.15% vs 0.13-0.14%).
- On **bank consolidation / M&A**: "prerogative of the Government of India" — not commenting; effectively standalone-for-now.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **ECL transition drag:** ~Rs.3,000-3,500 cr total; ~Rs.2,000-2,500 cr still to be absorbed (Rs.500-1,000 cr more this year) — a running credit-cost headwind (+~8-10 bps after tax on growth).
- **CASA at 39.73% vs 40% target** — "remains a challenge".
- **Geopolitical/MSME:** US-Iran-Israel / tariff overhang; MSME stress "not visible" but watchful; Rs.5,000 cr of ~Rs.11,000 cr eligible ECLGS already disbursed; one SMA-2 account (~Rs.190 cr, DCCO issue) expected to normalise on DCCO extension.
- **Competition:** "cut-throat" across home/vehicle/corporate loans for highly-rated accounts and good PSUs; home-loan rates ~7.15-7.20%, no bank leading rates lower.
- **March seasonality:** credit cost may spike again in March on audit factors (Q1's 0.23% is not the run-rate).
- **Treasury:** limited further yield tailwind (10Y ~6.65-6.75%).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - Confident, numbers-heavy, candid (MD explains why PCR wasn't pushed higher; flags March credit-cost seasonality; admits CASA is a grind). Consistent messaging that margins have bottomed and guidance sits at the upper end. MD left mid-call but EDs (Choudhury) handled detailed Q&A (SMA ticket sizes, LCR mechanics, provisioning reconciliation) credibly. Prudence bias: proactively over-provisioning ahead of ECL.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The bank is **deliberately front-loading ECL pain** (Rs.1,000 cr floating provision now, more to come) rather than waiting for the RBI transition — smoothing a ~Rs.3,000-3,500 cr hit so ongoing credit cost only rises ~8-10 bps.
- **Borrowings-over-bulk-deposits** funding strategy is the quiet NIM lever: TREPS/call at ~5.00-5.25% vs bulk at ~6.5-7%+; it also explains why LCR (123%) didn't rise despite the revised LCR norms (daily-repriced borrowings create daily outflows).
- Gold-loan growth guided **down to 15-16%** (from 26-28%) — last year's number was gold-**price** inflation, not tonnage; a read-through that gold-finance NBFCs' headline AUM growth is similarly price-flattered.
- **FCNR(B)/ECB USD1.5-2.0 bn** is a system-wide liquidity event (management sizes system inflow at USD50-70 bn ≈ Rs.4.5-7.0 lakh cr) that could cap G-Sec yields near 6.65%.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Capital position as on 30.06.2026: CRAR 17.58% (17.80% Jun-25, 17.93% Mar-26), with Total Capital of ₹79,121 Cr on Risk Weighted Assets of ₹4,50,043 Cr.
- Capital is almost entirely common equity — CET 1 capital of ₹74,319 Cr, Additional Tier I of nil (₹2,000 Cr a year earlier, now 0) and Tier II reduced to ₹4,802 Cr from ₹8,559 Cr in Jun-25.
- Risk-weight efficiency is improving: credit RWA density fell to 56.11% of gross advances from 58.68% a year earlier, with retail density at 55.91%, agriculture 23.99% and MSME the heaviest at 69.28%; market RWA density fell to 44.97% from 65.70%.
- Investment book is duration-managed and increasingly held-to-maturity: HTM rose 15.4% YoY to ₹1,64,948 Cr while AFS fell (12.0)% to ₹60,904 Cr; modified duration of AFS was 3.67 and of FVTPL including HFT was 1.07 (versus 3.19 a year earlier).
- Reserves & Surplus grew to ₹80,723 Cr from ₹71,327 Cr in Jun-25 on unchanged share capital of ₹1,347 Cr; book value per share stood at ₹510.72 versus ₹448.29 a year earlier.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body:
- **Deposits:** CASA +15.30% (current accounts +26.33% the standout); disciplined on bulk — prefers market borrowings at ~5.00-5.25% vs bulk deposits ~100-150 bps costlier.
- **Fee income:** driven by syndication fees ~Rs.72 cr, DEAF incentive Rs.30 cr, CBDC cost reimbursement ~Rs.47 cr; loan-processing charges up on **volume** (no rate hike) and called "sustainable".
- **Treasury:** AFS reserve +Rs.544 cr to +Rs.503 cr; treasury profit modest, annual assumption Rs.600-700 cr.
- **International:** FCNR(B)/ECB mobilisation USD1.5-2.0 bn; overseas incl. Singapore; funding cost not materially lower (~6.0-6.5% deposit-equivalent).

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Government of India holds 73.84% of the Bank as on 30.06.26; the balance 26.16% is public and others, including mutual funds 13.52%, FPI/FII/NRI & AIF 6.27% and insurance companies 3.42%.
- Business mix is deliberately RAM-led: RAM share of domestic advances rose from 65.34% (Jun-25) to 66.00% (Jun-26), with the portfolio split as Retail 23%, Agriculture 25%, MSME 18% and Corporate 34% as on 30.06.2026.
- Distribution is pan-India and rural-weighted: 6003 domestic branches (Rural 2011 / 33%, Semi-urban 1606 / 27%, Metro 1191 / 20%, Urban 1195 / 20%) plus 3 overseas branches and 1 IBU (GIFT City branch), and 28,994 pan-India touch points.
- The deck states the Bank surpassed all mandatory RBI targets under Priority Sector advances, with achievement (excluding PSLC) of 45.36% of ANBC against a 40.00% benchmark, agriculture 21.44% vs 18.00%, micro under MSME 11.59% vs 7.50% and non-corporate farmers 20.67% vs 14.00%.
- External credit ratings: S&P Global Ratings issuer rating BBB/Stable/A-2; domestically CRISIL rates Tier 2 AA+/Stable, Infrastructure Bond AAA/Stable and Certificate of Deposit A1+, with CARE assigning AAA/Stable issuer rating.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Asset quality] GNPA of ₹12,710 Cr / 1.86% and NNPA of ₹990 Cr / 0.15% as on 30.06.2026, with PCR of 98.22% including technical write-off and 92.21% excluding it; gross NPA has fallen from ₹18,067 Cr (Jun-25) on fresh slippages of ₹1,250 Cr against reductions of ₹1,780 Cr in the quarter.
- [Stressed exposure] NCLT accounts with the Bank total 284 accounts / ₹22,114 Cr exposure carrying 100% provision (PCR 100%); 14 accounts with book balance ₹3,998 Cr have been acquired by NARCL, and the Bank has invested ₹272.25 Cr face value in NARCL and ₹1.00 Cr in IDRCL as equity.
- [Early warning] SMA (₹5 Cr and above) fell sharply to ₹1,715 Cr or 0.26% of standard advances as on 30.06.2026, from ₹5,791 Cr / 0.99% a year earlier, with corporate & others down from ₹3,480 Cr to ₹340 Cr.
- [Group entities] A general insurance joint venture (consortium of Indian public and private corporates with Sompo of Japan as promoter, incorporated and licensed in 2007) in which the Bank holds 28.52% reported Gross Direct Premium of ₹1,751 Cr in Q1FY27, up 34% YoY, with net profit after tax of ₹59 Cr; a listed stock broking & DP subsidiary, 64.84% held, reported Stock Broking Income of ₹358 Cr in Q1FY27, down (4)% YoY; a wholly owned subsidiary incorporated on 09.02.2024 with ₹10 Cr authorised and paid-up capital is to offer outsourcing solutions for banking operations, and reported Q1FY27 net profit of ₹14.58 lakh.
- [Sponsored RRBs] Tamil Nadu Grama Bank and Puducherry Grama Bank together had business of ₹63,290 Cr (+14% YoY) and 748 branches, but combined operating profit fell (49)% to ₹297 Cr and net profit (49)% to ₹185 Cr, with Tamil Nadu Grama Bank net profit down (57)% YoY.
- [Financial inclusion schemes] ₹466.52 Cr of IND MSME Digi loans disbursed to 1,731 beneficiaries cumulatively till 30.06.26; PM SVANidhi ₹1,295 Cr to 8.06 lakh beneficiaries and PM Vishwakarma ₹98 Cr to 13,825 beneficiaries since inception; SHG disbursements of ₹4,044 Cr in Q1FY27 across 5.01 lakh SHGs financed; average balance in PMJDY accounts of ₹5,517 versus the industry's ₹5,224.
- [Awards] SKOCH Golden Award for IB SAATHI and SKOCH Silver for Security Operations, Financial Express Best PSB Award 2024-25, Golden Peacock Award for Excellence in Artificial Intelligence-2026, APY Annual Award of Excellence for achieving 104% of the FY26 APY target, and CIBIL's Best Data Quality Award.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body:
- NIM +6 bps QoQ (domestic & global). Cost of deposits fell despite early-quarter tightening — driven by CASA focus, bulk-deposit discipline and cheaper market borrowings; deposit repricing added ~1-1.5 bps.
- Yield on advances +~2 bps; further term-deposit repricing pending (~2-3 bps benefit). Mgmt view: margins have bottomed, no major trigger up or down → broadly stable, upper end of 3.15-3.25% achievable.
- Cost-to-income down to 44.80% (from ~46%); ECL adoption will lift standard-asset provisioning from ~0.4-0.5% to ~1.5% (i.e. ~+1% on incremental growth, ~8-10 bps on credit cost after tax).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** PAT Rs.3,273 cr (+10.09% YoY), OP Rs.5,557 cr (+16.51%), NII +~17% YoY, NIM +6 bps, ROE 19.48%, C/I 44.80%. Deposits +13.40% / advances +13.89% (Rs.6.85 lakh cr), CASA +15.30%. GNPA 1.86% (−115 bps YoY), NNPA 0.15%, PCR 98.22%, credit cost 0.23%, slippage 0.77%. CAR 17.58% / CET1 16.51%. Took Rs.1,000 cr floating ECL provision (total transition ~Rs.3,000-3,500 cr); reaffirmed FY27 guidance at upper end (NIM 3.15-3.25%, GNPA 1.50-1.60%, recovery Rs.4,500-5,500 cr, CASA 40%, credit growth 13-14%, FCNR/ECB USD1.5-2.0 bn).
- _Next Q → check: NIM at upper end of 3.15-3.25%? GNPA toward 1.50-1.60%? further ECL provision (Rs.500-1,000 cr) taken? CASA progress to 40%? agri growth back to 15-16%? FCNR(B)/ECB drawdown & deployment; MSME/ECLGS stress emergence._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
- **Credit growth FY27:** balanced ~13-14% (would allow advances +15% if deposits +13%, without compromising NIM); mgmt notes RAM alone can do 17-18% if agri returns to 16%.
- **NIM FY27:** guidance **3.15-3.25%**; **upper end achievable**; MCLR repricing drag (~2 bps) offset by bulk-deposit repricing benefit (~2-3 bps) → broadly stable to +2-3 bps.
- **Gross NPA target:** **1.50-1.60%** ("no challenge in achieving that").
- **Recovery target FY27:** **Rs.4,500-5,500 cr**; ~Rs.1,900 cr already achieved in Q1.
- **CASA ratio target:** **40%** (39.73% reached; "CASA remains a challenge").
- **Cost-to-income:** ~45% range.
- **Agriculture growth:** back to **15-16%** (Q1 was 9.96% on jewel-loan IT/transition drag).
- **Gold-loan growth:** ~**15-16%** this year (vs 26-28% last year, which was price- not tonnage-driven; comfortable LTV even after ~30% gold-price move).
- **FCNR(B)+ECB mobilisation:** **USD1.5-2.0 billion** (~Rs.18,000 cr liquidity); USD150 mn raised so far, USD1 bn pipeline.
- **ECL transition:** total impact ~**Rs.3,000-3,500 cr**; Rs.1,000 cr provided in Q1; will provide another **Rs.500-1,000 cr** this year; steady-state credit cost +~8-10 bps after tax on incremental growth.
- **Treasury profit FY27:** annual plan assumes only ~**Rs.600-700 cr** (10Y G-Sec ~6.65-6.75%, limited further downside).
- **Digital/IT budget FY27:** ~**Rs.750 cr** capital budget for AI + cyber resilience; total IT budget (capex+opex) ~**Rs.3,000 cr**.
- Overall: "maintaining all guidance … expect performance towards the **upper end** of the guided ranges."
outlook.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)

outlook.body:
- Advances ~Rs.6.85 lakh cr, +13.89%. Mix: **RAM 66%** (Retail +18.74%, Agri +9.96%, MSME +17%), Corporate +11.49%.
- Domestic CD ratio 78.66%; global CD ratio 81.06%. Domestic CASA ratio +6 bps QoQ / +~76 bps YoY.
- **Shed ~Rs.6,000 cr** of highly-competitive/thinly-priced loans (pricing discipline); NBFC book +2% YoY (added ~Rs.3,000 cr in Q1 after a ~Rs.6,000-7,000 cr run-off; selective, AAA/AA only).
- Jewel-loan (gold) book **Rs.1.32 lakh cr**. Bulk deposits flat at ~Rs.1.61 lakh cr (stayed out when CD/bulk rates hit 7.7-8.0%).
- Branch participation improving: **51% of branches hit targets** (vs 25-27% a year ago).
outlook.title: Loan book & growth mix (pipeline)

outlook.body:
- **RAM-led growth** (66% of book) with Retail +18.74% / MSME +17% as the durable engine; agri to re-accelerate to 15-16% once jewel-loan IT/transition normalises.
- **International / FCNR(B)-ECB** (USD1.5-2.0 bn) opens overseas deployment optionality (Singapore + domestic redeployment of ~Rs.18,000 cr liquidity).
- **Fee/syndication income** scaling (syndication ~Rs.72 cr this quarter) — underwriting/syndication franchise called "sustainable"; DEAF/CBDC incentives add non-linear fee optionality.
- **Digital/AI build-out** (data lakehouse, UEBA, zero-trust) positions for cost-to-income efficiency; ECLGS re-launch (~Rs.11,000 cr eligible) is a downside cushion, not growth.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: A clean, and asset quality still improving. Management is trading a little near-term margin/growth for balance-sheet strength, building an ECL buffer and shedding thinly-priced loans, while reaffirming FY27 guidance and pointing to the **upper end** of most ranges.
